_rules.attested: A name canon gives is landed on the graph entity the geometry supports (docs/research/phase16/16g-mining.md §1.1). One name may sit on several river ids when canon describes one river: those entries share a `chain`.
_rules.extrapolated: Every river with strahler >= 2 or accumKm2 >= 4, every body of 1 ha or more, every lagoon, and every vertical-fall reach that canon does not name takes a name in the naming register of the culture territory at its centre (world/sources/catalogue/README.md, 'Per-region naming register'). The territory is read from the published soc-cultures.png; where the centre is unclaimed hinterland the nearest claimed cell is used.
_rules.catalogue: A water smaller than the extrapolation rule is named only when a live catalogue place record already names it and stands within 150 m of it.
_rules.peak: A summit site in world/sources/sites/candidate-sites.json with scores.prominenceM >= 60 that is the highest such summit within 600 m: one name per massif.
_rules.pass: No saddle site lies within 60 m of a published major road (the nearest is 87 m), so passes are taken along the roads instead: the point of greatest ground height on each published route, when that point is interior to the route, stands above sea level and the route descends at least 10 m on both sides of it. Two routes qualify. The 10 m descent is the one threshold this rule adds beyond the brief and it is the single constant to change if the owner wants more passes.
_rules.style: No two names are identical unless they share a `chain`; the imagery words reed, root, water, stone, shadow, blood and bone appear at most twice per register; verb-clause shares are taken from the per-region naming register in world/sources/catalogue/README.md, so saxhleel-coast (the hyphenated-verb register at its purest) needs at least half its names as clauses and every other register at most a third; capitalisation follows docs/standards/text/style-guide.md 1.3.
_rules.graph: hydrology-graph.json is NOT edited: its contentSha256 is recorded downstream by carve_province and compile_water, so this record stays beside the graph and readers join on entityId.
_rules.textKey: Every name is a text-catalogue entry keyed text.hydrology.name.<entityId>. The brief asked for hydrology.name.<entityId>; the catalogue's TEXT_ID_SHAPE (standard 4) requires the text. prefix, so the prefix is added and nothing else changed.
